page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1620.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0, both falling in the average range. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3703.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3324.57, which place it in the bottom 25% of tested configurations.

Memory performance represents a significant bottleneck for this instance type. The Passmark memory score of 989.87 is in the bottom 10%, and uncached read and write memory bandwidths are limited to 27.54 GB/sec and 21.03 GB/sec respectively. Despite these memory constraints, the hardware-assisted encryption capabilities perform adequately, achieving an average rating in the Passmark CPU encryption test. LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model show an average text generation speed of 112.59 tokens/sec, though prompt processing speeds remain weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 offers dedicated compute resources with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a specialized option for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. However, the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth limit its utility for memory-intensive databases or heavy parallel processing. The instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, basic text processing, and entry-level utility workloads.
